correctness.rationale: Every complex vector is dominated by a nonnegative real vector for both positive shift correlations. The parity blocks of Re(J^2) are two paths; even dimensions have two independent top Perron vectors with a strictly positive Re(J) cross term. Odd dimensions have a simple top eigenvalue with positive gap; the variational threshold is bounded. Three-dimensional scalar maximization is exact. Five-dimensional reflection positivity, exact factorization and negative discriminant prove the global sharp inequality, matched by two-block infinitesimal perturbations. Exact algebraic identities independently replayed by the embedded checker. The n^(3/2) two-sided order follows from explicit sine eigenvectors and cosine expansions; no computation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full published primary literature and current 2026 motivating preprint were compared by their mathematical statements, not titles. Existing broad operator inequalities do not determine nonlinear saturation for these two powers, and KMS numerical-range results concern a distinct single combined operator. Targeted published published-finding corpus searches had no covering claim. An unindexed equivalent theorem remains an acknowledged originality risk.
residual_risks: A differently worded pre-existing joint numerical range result outside indexed or accessible sources may imply the exact thresholds.
Published search corpus cannot establish global uniqueness or expose unpublished work.
Only inspected material, not every page of every historical paper, was compared; conclusions are scoped to material read.

value.rationale: The classical nilpotent Jordan contraction and its first two powers are canonical test operators for joint numerical radius. The theorem gives a structural parity-dependent phase transition, two exact critical parameters, and the nontrivial n^(3/2) asymptotic scale. These are not generic textbook consequences of independent operator-radius bounds and require a sharp global polynomial inequality in dimension five.
